title: New dissector: ILDA Digital Network (IDN) Protocol
description:
Stream Specification: https://www.ilda.com/resources/StandardsDocs/ILDA_IDN-Stream_rev001.pdf

The stream specification only defines IDN messages. The other packet commands
like ping request, ping response, etc. (see line 25 - 31 in packet-idn.c)
are part of the hello specification which is not released yet. We were still
able to implement some hello packets since we received a preliminary version
of the hello specification, because we need the hello packets for our work.

Gerrit History: https://code.wireshark.org/review/#/c/37333/

If you are sure, then please remove this check and we can re-fuzz.  I can't remember if it actually came in with that value.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/300/diffs?diff_id=112303667&start_sha=2ba163160baab1cc5c69e6f6bdfd0f53491dc5db#e02e1da3dbd02f0c5554830710fdeddb717e6bbb_530_534)
Again, I grew this to avoid a valgrind error when I got a fuzzed config message.

Hi Maxim, glad to see this uploaded.  My comments are really just checking on your last comments from gerrit.  If you decide what you want to do with those comments (including some where I may have broken things), I can do a fresh review.

I definitely saw from fuzzing that if the config message had junk values in it, the code could still get confused when it tried to use those values, so might need more checks to ignore obviously wrong config frames?

Hey Martin,

yeah, the config messages define how the data in all following packets is parsed, so if the configuration header is changed in the fuzzing process, then errors are inevitable. I guess in this case it actually makes sense to just set word_count=255 at the dic_precision allocation to avoid errors. I will fix the other two cases and make a new commit.

So somehow we managed to try to use a fuzzed config frame which resulted in trying to divide by a zero config->sample_size.  Could either:
- test here, and exist early (maybe with expert info)
- mark the corresponding field in the config frame as invalid (with expert info), and don't store for frames like this to look and and use.
